summary: Kenryu Nishio studied at Otani University, earning a doctorate in literature. A specialist in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology, he served as professor emeritus at Hanazono University (attested 2014 and 2026).
Kenryu T. Tsuji worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed studies at Ryukoku University in 1938 and also studied at the University of Toronto.

Kenryu Tsukinowa studied at Bukkyo University and worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held professorships at Koyasan University (1926), Seizan College, and Shuchiin University (1955), later serving as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University in 1956.

Kenshi Kusano is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University from circa 1971 to 1975 and later served as a professor there from circa 1996 to 2018.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Kensur Yeshe Thupten served in 1982 as a visiting Tibetan scholar at the University of Virginia and held a post at Middlebury College that same year. He taught numerous scholars, including Donald S. Lopez Jr.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Kenta Suzuki studied at Kyoto University (~1994–1998) and the University of Tokyo (~1998–2004). He served as an associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College around 2013.

Kenyo Mitomo studied at Rissho University and UC Berkeley. A specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held appointments including Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University (1968–2015) and visiting professor at UC Berkeley (1987).

Keshub Chunder Sen worked in religious studies and Indology, and founded the Brahmo Samaj. He was educated at the Hindu School, Presidency College, Kolkata (~1856–1858), and the University of Calcutta (~1857–1858).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Kevin Alan Vose studied at Bates College and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD in 2005 under Jeffrey Hopkins. He also studied under traditional teacher Ngawang Jinpa.
Kevin Buckelew works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Sarah Lawrence College, with doctoral supervision by Chun-fang Yu, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang.
Kexin Zheng is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. As of 2026, Zheng is a PhD candidate at Leiden University studying under doctoral supervisor Peter Bisschop.

Khakyab Dorje was active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and later taught figures such as Kalu Rinpoche and Pema Wangchok Gyelpo.

Khammai Dhammasami earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford (~1999–2004). A Buddhist studies scholar, he served as Oxford's Buddhist chaplain, abbot of Oxford Buddha Vihara, and professor at International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University.
Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Jampal Gyepe Dorje and Akyong Tokden Lodrö Gyatso.
Khantipālo studied under teachers including Sangharakshita (~1960–1963), Dhardo Rinpoche, Namkhai Norbu, and Dudjom Rinpoche. He also taught Ayya Khema.
Khenchen Ngawang Khyen Rab Gyatso was an individual who studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Trulshik Rinpoche.
Khenchen Tashi Özer studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He later taught Khakyab Dorje and Pema Wangchok Gyelpo.

Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche studied under Khenpo Gangshar and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he served as abbot of Rumtek Monastery (~1960), Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (~1981), and Gampo Abbey (~1984–2023).
Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Khenpo Appey Rinpoche studied at Dzongsar Monastery and under Dragyab Lodrö. Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he served as director of Sakya College from 1972 to 1985 and held a post at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.
